content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a Self-Architectural Knowledge Distillation framework (SAKD) which migrates the knowledge from ANN to SNN with the same architecture. The authors utilize the single-stage one-shot NAS to explore the effect of SNN with different architectures on transferring knowledge with fixed ANN. Then they find that the teacher model does not favor a particular student architecture and use the teacher and student model with the same architecture will achieve better performance. This method combines two knowledge distillation strategies: logits knowledge distillation and feature knowledge distillation. In the experiments, the authors verify the high performance of this method on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, ImageNet and DVS-CIFAR10 dataset. Besides, the authors visualize the intermediate layer and the gradient-weighted class activation mapping of ANNs and SNNs.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
(1) This paper explores the impact of different architectures on knowledge distillation with one-shot NAS and finds that choose ANNs with the same architecture as SNNs bring more significant improvement to the student model.
(2) This paper combines two knowledge distillation strategies: logits knowledge distillation and feature knowledge distillation and achieves high performance compared with other SOTA learning algorithms.
(3) The visualization of the intermediate layer and the gradient-weighted class activation mapping shows that the SNN’s features more informative through learning the knowledge from ANNs.
Weaknesses:
(1) In the experiments, the table 2 shows that the accuracy of different teachers for SNNs, but the accuracy of using the same ANN architectures as SNN is not significantly higher than other teacher architectures. Maybe more experiments can be done to prove that.
(2) The accuracy of only use the surrogate gradient method to training SNN and the accuracy of ANN can be added to verify this method more clarity.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This work is very useful and valuable. It is novel to training SNN by transferring the knowledge from the teacher ANN to student SNN. This method combines the typical cross-entropy loss and the loss of feature and logits distillation which make the SNN learn the knowledge from the intermediate layer and the output layer. Moreover, the authors explore how to choose the structure of ANN and SNN to efficiently transfer knowledge from ANN to SNN. In a word, this article is clarity and of high quality.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposes a new method for training SNN which is transferring the knowledge from the teacher ANN to student SNN. What’s more, the authors find that the teacher model does not favor a particular student architecture. Choosing the same teacher architecture as the student will be simpler and achieve high performance. Then they verify this method on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, ImageNet and DVS-CIFAR10 and compare with some other SOTA learning algorithms. In conclusion, the research of this article is very valuable.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper presents a distillation based spiking neural network training strategy to improve classification performance. Results on cifar, imagenet and dvs dataset show that the proposed method can boost the accuracy while mitigating the accuracy gap with conventional ANN.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
### Strengths:

1. The results are very strong.
2. The general idea of distillation to boost accuracy is clear.

### Weakness:

The paper uses well known techniques of conventional ANN like attention transfer based distillation, self distillation to use in the proposed method.

The L_feaKD is same as AT loss. Morever, in the SNN paradigm as well, this loss was leveraged to boost accuracy, please refer to [1].

The NAS part is not clear at all. Also, that part is not new, it has largely followed traditional once for all training framework.

The NAS part is written in a hurried way without clearly mentioning the reason of it's existence. Finally the inference from table 2 is what the authors leveraged. Though I strongly doubt the fact that self distillation is the best way to distill even if we can afford a larger ANN.

Please clarify if the training was done with rate or direct coded inputs.


[1] Spike-Thrift: Towards Energy-Efficient Deep Spiking Neural Networks by Limiting Spiking Activity via Attention-Guided Compression, WACV 2021.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors discuss the choice of architecture and the design of knowledge distillation from ANN to SNN. At first, an ANN is trained and then multiple sampled SNNs are trained to select the best student model. The authors discover that SNN does not prefer changing its architecture while doing KD. Thus, the same architecture with ANN is retained for SNN.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

1. It studies a particular paradigm, that is, when doing KD if the SNN has its preference in choosing the architecture.

2. Their experiments seem to be thorough for reaching high performance.

Weakness: 

1. The setup in this paper does not really convince me. First, I am unsure why the KD has to be added to SNN training. If we match the outputs from ANN and SNN even for intermediate features, there could be no advantage of temporal features in SNNs. Second, the authors claim that SNN's architecture should not be changed. But the source ANN architecture is fixed, in that case, the full search space for ANN and SNN is not explored. 

2. Using KD to achieve higher performance is not fair compared to existing methods, which require an already trained ANN and consume more computations.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Clarity, quality, and novelty are fair in this paper. Code is provided for reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: To summarize, this paper studies the SNN from a particular perspective so that it cannot be generalized to standard training settings. Thus, I recommend the rejection of this submission.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper introduces neural architecture search (NAS) and find that the performance is insensitive to the architectures of SNNs. By choosing the same architecture for ANN-teacher and SNN-student, the paper thus propose a Self-Architectural Knowledge Distillation framework (SAKD), which transfers the knowledge (i.e., the features and logits) of ANNs to that of SNNs with the same architecture. The experiments show that they can achieve state-of-the-art performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength

1. The paper study an interesting problem that use NAS to convert ANN to SNN.
2. The experiments show good results. 


Weaknesses
1. The proposed teacher training training method is not novel, as it already exists in deep learning in many years.
2. The result that the performance is insensitive to the architectures of SNNs is really counter intuitive. I somewhat doubt the whether the authors have done a thorough NAS. The authors should discuss the limit of the proposed method.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is clearly written. The quality is good. The novelty is limited. It is reproducible as the code is provided
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper address an interesting problem for ANN to SNN. And the experiments show good results. But the proposed method is limited novel, and it fails to discuss its limitation.
